note: No claims. All 157 pivots are Middle Irish (mostly OCR'd journal texts: RC, ZCP, Félire), and the partners are mostly Greek prose; almost every bundle shares only vocabulary. Leads I looked at and dropped as institutional or generic, not phraseological: (1) BC-314d7, bride-wealth of cattle and horses: Esnada Tige Buchet 'bóin ⁊ dam, ech ⁊ ór ⁊ argat' beside Palaephatus 23 'ἵππους ... βοῦς' (cf. Il. 11.244); the cognate livestock words name the same institution but share no wording. (2) BC-22de8, Hesiod fr. 199.10 'ἔεδνα δίδον' beside Notker's Martianus 'ze uuídemen ze gébenne': ἕδνον ~ widamo is a cognate noun for the bride-gift, but 'give' is the default verb, the verbs are not cognate, and Notker is translating Latin. (3) BC-bd395 and BC-c26e0, milking cows into a stream (Findglais) beside the Testament of Job (mligid~ἀμέλγω, bó~βοῦς, sruth~ῥέω): a natural pastoral collocation, and the Greek text is not inherited. (4) Lists of domestic animals, tears running over the face, hazel and ash (from the translated Tristrams saga).
